facebook.content_angle: Breathing pattern and oxygen debt — how breathing every stroke in the final 25m costs more time than most swimmers realise, and the controlled breathing strategy elite swimmers use to hold speed through the finish
facebook.post_text:
Gasping for air in the final 25m is costing you more than you think. 🫁

Most club swimmers start panic-breathing every stroke when the pain hits — and that single habit breaks body position, kills rotation, and bleeds speed exactly when the race is decided.

👉 Every extra breath disrupts your stroke cycle and adds drag at the worst possible moment
👉 Elite swimmers rehearse a controlled breathing pattern in training so the final 25m feels familiar under pressure
👉 Reducing to a 2-stroke breathing cycle in the last length — not eliminating breaths — keeps oxygen flowing without wrecking your line

The swimmers holding their best split to the wall aren't tougher. They're better prepared. 🔥

✔️ Practice your race breathing pattern in every threshold set — not just on race day
✔️ Build tolerance with a descending breathing drill: breath every 3, every 4, every 5 across 200m repeats
✔️ Your body already knows how to finish fast — train the pattern until the pain can't change it
